column1: # Documented "different engine" exceptions (PHASE4.md): one per line, numbers from the oracle (SF19 Lite vs SF16 d22) and the chess.com rule that explains the difference.

column4: different top move: 9...Bxg4 and 9...Nxg4 both take the blundered queen; SF16 d22 Bxg4 -578 vs Nxg4 -574 (4 cp), SF19 d22 Nxg4 -758 first, Lite mpv5 rank 2 (dump Bxg4 -7.63 vs Nxg4 -7.23); chess.com labels Bxg4 Excellent = not its top move, and Great needs the top move. Punish-a-blunder Great (rating 243) is right for whichever capture is the engine top.

different engine at the B-E3 boundary: 25.Rd5 (rook en prise, sacrifice 5) is not the top move; SF19 Lite d1d4 +1.08 vs Rd5 +0.74 = loss 0.0313 > 0.03 at 1660, SF16 d22 d1d4 +107 vs Rd5 +77 (rank 2) = loss 0.027 < 0.03, so on chess.com's engine numbers our rules give Brilliant.

chess.com's own engine disagrees with its label: SF16 d22 ranks 12.Bxb5 outside its top 5 (f1h3 +380 ... Bxb5 +299, loss 0.043 at 562/floor 800), SF19 d22 too, Lite mpv5 rank 5; no rule on Stockfish numbers can call it near-best.

different top move: SF16 d22 g6f5 +327 vs e1c1 +310 (17 cp), fresh SF19 Lite ranks e1c1 first; chess.com labels 17.Bf5 Excellent (not its top move), our dump has it top so the (fake, regain 4 for 2) bishop offer passes B-E4 margin 5.
